text: The hypothesis is confirmed and the contract works, but integrating it into instant closure collides with a frozen oracle, so the repair is returned rather than sealed. Confirmation first: before the contract, a single simulation in a fresh process performed 49 AVAILABLE planning reads while it ran and two more landed after simulate() had returned; four runs gave 49, 51, 51, 51 as each generation inherited the previous one's late reads. With OwnerKeyReconcileQueue.awaitCurrentWorkIdle() - idle iff draining false, pending empty, inFlight empty - delegated through UnifiedRebalancer and consumed as one more explicit owner in the instant-closure fixpoint, every run performs exactly 45 reads, none land after the scenario returns, and the attribution gate's foreign-skip count falls from 106 to 1. Q1 to Q5 pass, including the draining clause and the ABA boundary; test/workflow is 436 green and test/rebalancer 6801 green, so the production API and the delegation are inert on their own. The blocker is the 429-entry metered scheduler and pass oracle. With the rebalancer owners withheld from the closure set it is 429 and identical across runs; with them in it becomes 413 on the first run and 391 on every later run, reproducibly. Awaiting the planner's accepted work at each instant legitimately changes how much is admitted per instant, so the oracle moved - and it also made the first run differ from later runs in the metered trace, where previously they agreed. That is an owner decision: either the previous closure was under-draining and the oracle must be re-baselined, or the contract belongs at a different boundary.
